newsitem.title: TAIWAN: U.S. House speaker Gingrich arrives in Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House speaker Gingrich arrives in Taiwan.

text.p: U.S. congressional chief Newt Gingrich arrived in Taiwan on Wednesday for three-hour visit, getting a hero's welcome after asserting that U.S. forces would defend the island against attack by communist China.

Gingrich, the first speaker of the House of Representatives to visit since Washington switched diplomatic ties to Beijing in 1979, landed at a Taipei military base aboard a U.S. military transport to conclude a blunt-speaking Asian tour that included stops in South Korea, Hong Kong, China and Japan.

Gingrich shook hands warmly with foreign minister John Chang and a host of other Taiwan officials as well as leaders of Washington's de facto embassy, the private but government-funded American Institute in Taiwan.
He made no comment to reporters before being whisked away by limousine for a meeting with President Lee Teng-hui and a lunch with Vice President and cabinet chief Lien Chan.

Though Gingrich planned to stay only three hours, his visit was deeply symbolic, spotlighting Taiwan's 48-year estrangement from China as well as delicate U.S. policy toward Taiwan, seen by Beijing as the key irritant in Sino-U.S. ties.

Gingrich said after a weekend Beijing visit that he had told China's communist leader that U.S. forces would defend Taiwan in the face of attack by Beijing -- something Washington has not explicitly promised to do.
